# Unpublished cloud integration candidate — Step 25

## Release boundary

This candidate is development preparation, not production activation. All five release controls are false: LEGACY_CLOUD_ENABLED, CRM_READ_FEATURES_ENABLED, CRM_WRITES_ENABLED, PRIVATE_MEDIA_ENABLED and CLOUD_TRANSFER_ENABLED. Guards reject unauthorized users before gates; locked authorized requests return 423 before bodies or storage bindings. No browser parameter or environment variable overrides a gate.

The existing browser CRM app.js is byte-identical to Version 15. Its storage key, safe startup, explicit save and confirmed restore remain intact. A navigation link opens a separate owner-protected /workspace-cloud page. That page performs no requests at startup and never reads or writes localStorage. Cloud refresh and edits are explicit; no automatic merging or switching exists.

## Implemented code paths (tested with synthetic fixtures only)

- Inventory, customer and enquiry creates/updates; original payload fields retained on update.
- Sale creation uses explicit sale ID, validates vehicle availability and preserves IDs. Initial receipts require payment method and atomically enter payment history and cashbook. Subsequent payments reduce matching recorded balances in sale and vehicle, without recomputing historical balances from old receipt totals.
- Expense totals update parking/other components once, with integer-cent arithmetic and revision control. Repairs remain separate from vehicle costs; no automatic double counting.
- Location/parking spot, document requirements/expiry, inspection, reservation, RTO/HPA, repair, reminder, follow-up, cashbook and price-change write services. Cashbook payments and vehicle costs must use their dedicated flows.
- Transactional global revision CAS and per-payload revision increments, unique database constraints, fingerprinted idempotency receipts, audit log and vehicle timeline. A retry after uncertain response must resend the identical command/token. No bulk delete or destructive replacement API.
- Existing 27-table cloud reads, manual pagination and record editing UI. Append-only financial/history records cannot be silently rewritten.
- Media file selection/camera attributes, private upload, stable-token retry, list, JPEG/PNG/WebP preview, download, archive/unarchive and staged-upload reconciliation. Sold-vehicle associations retained. No object deletion or public URLs.
- Import preview classifies every vehicle and enquiry, flags duplicate keys and revision conflicts, and lists existing sale IDs for reconciliation. It never writes.
- Transactional 27-table database snapshot export with SHA-256, bounded at 5,000 rows/table and 20 MiB. API verifies structure/checksum. `node scripts/verify-cloud-restore.mjs SNAPSHOT.json` additionally rehearses schema, constraints, foreign keys and full row roundtrip in an in-memory SQLite database. No hosted writes.

## Deliberately incomplete / activation blockers

- Real business import execution and cloud cutover are NOT implemented. The browser backup has vehicle records and embedded sale information, not a complete explicit cloud sale/customer ID mapping. Those identities and conflict choices require a reviewed mapping, migration implementation and transactional tests before importing. Never invent replacements for historical IDs.
- Hosted database restore and full R2 disaster restore/bulk export have not been implemented or rehearsed. Independent file exports and the recovery runbook are available; a D1 snapshot alone cannot restore file bytes.
- The original browser-local forms do not switch to cloud persistence. Persistent operations use the separate explicit workspace; original dashboards continue to summarize local records. No automatic synchronization, offline cloud queue or cross-device background refresh.
- Existing sales cannot be amended/reversed, payments cannot be refunded/edited and cashbook entries are append-only. Separate reconciliation workflows are required for corrections. Review-status vehicles require reconciliation before sale. Reservations are not automatically converted on sale.
- Inspection/auction/age-baseline writes have service support but no dedicated workspace forms. Owner preferences and generated documents have reads only; no document generation or automated notifications.
- Media PDF/HEIC previews, HEIC conversion, malware scanning, multipart resume, bulk recovery and client revision tokens for cover/archive are not implemented. Archive/cover last-writer behavior is documented; no media-byte deletion occurs.
- Live hosted identity/header protection, owner subject pinning, actual iPhone camera behavior, real D1/R2 bindings and complete end-to-end hosted flows remain unverified. DOM mocks validate UI contracts, not browser rendering.

## Separate production approvals required

1. Confirm the target live D1 resource and migration ledger; do not assume empty. Review the restored immutable nine-table + eighteen-table migrations. Approve provisioning/connection and migrations explicitly.
2. Approve private R2 provisioning/binding; verify no public bucket exposure. Confirm storage/export/restore support and limits.
3. Authorize a gated deployment of this exact cloud candidate only after platform/database review. Its manifest requests DB and BUCKET; it is not covered by prior UI-only release approval. All gates remain false even after that deployment.
4. Under separate authorization, enable only the reviewed reads/writes/media/transfer capabilities and test owner/non-owner protection with isolated temporary records. Verify hosted transaction and retry semantics.
5. Complete and test explicit historical ID mapping/import, get a fresh owner backup, preview actual target conflicts, approve import and manual cutover separately. Do not overwrite localStorage.

## Recovery baseline

Version 15: appgprj_6aca62581e288191af74309f0392facc~appgver_36bb42294c848191bf2419287b9ab90a; commit 6235df3bd9ebc0b4a1fd03d5a043e7477a25544f. Its safe browser-local code is retained. Reverting application code does not undo D1 migrations or R2 changes. Preserve independent database/media backups and avoid automatic rollback to Version 4, whose legacy startup could transform browser records.

# Dealer Desk local browser backup — Stage 2 migration safety checkpoint

**Scope:** Read-only structural review of the owner's existing `naina-motors-backup-2026-10-11(2).json`, available only in the local conversation environment. **The actual backup, buyer names, registration numbers, chassis/engine details, phone numbers, and original vehicle IDs were NOT committed, uploaded, sent to GitHub, or imported into D1.** The original source file was not changed.

## Local results

- Backup format: **version 3**; `validateBackup` from the unchanged CRM cloud-core returned **zero structural errors**.
- Vehicle count: **386**, all with nonempty original IDs.
- Status counts: **325 Sold**, **58 Available**, **3 Review**.
- Duplicate exact vehicle IDs, normalized usable registrations, or chassis numbers found in this offline backup: **0**.
- Sold vehicles missing buyer name: **18**. Historical values must be preserved; never fabricate a customer.
- Sold records missing selling price: **0**.
- Sold records missing recorded sale date: **0**.
- Sale balance exceeding sale price: **0**.
- Inconsistent combined parking/other expense totals: **0**.
- Missing separate parking/other expense fields: **0**.
- Leads in this backup: **0** (not proof that no cloud lead records exist).
- `planImport` generated an **empty-cloud hypothetical preview** with **386 candidate vehicle inserts** and **3 Review-status warnings**. This was NOT a comparison against actual production/staging D1 and did NOT execute an import.

## Critical unresolved migration mapping

1. **Preserve all original vehicle IDs and payload/source rows**. The 18 sold entries without buyer names remain sold records; they must not become new fake or duplicate customer entities.
2. **Historical sale IDs/customer IDs** must be reconciled against any pre-existing D1 rows. Browser backup buyer fields and legacy `sourceSales` cannot be assumed to be independently assigned normalized D1 sales or customers. Never invent a new historical sale ID silently or double-count payments.
3. The three `Review` vehicles remain unchanged pending the owner's source-document review.
4. An actual hosted, authenticated D1 import preview with a known current global revision is required. The empty-database synthetic preview does not authorize a transaction.
5. Take and verify both a full original browser JSON backup and independent D1/R2 recoverable backups BEFORE any live data copy. No production databases/files were changed during this checkpoint.

## Reproduce safely

```sh
node scripts/audit-local-backup.mjs /path/to/your-private-browser-backup.json
```

The command performs **local reads only** and prints an aggregate JSON report, including SHA-256 of the source bytes to identify the exact backup copy. It does not output names, registration numbers, chassis or vehicle IDs, or write a file. The CLI and pure engine are covered by `tests/browser-backup-audit.test.mjs` using **fictional test data only**.

**Status:** Backup structure checked; migration *not ready* until true historical sale/customer mapping, hosted D1 reads and rollback proof are complete.

## Historical source-sheet fidelity gate

A deeper **local-only** comparison of the preserved source spreadsheet rows against the corresponding normalized backup fields established:
- All **325 Sold** vehicles have a matching source-sales status `SOLD`; all **58 Available** vehicles have source-sales status `UNSOLD`.
- The **3 Review** vehicles have deliberately conflicting original sheets: inventory marks them sold but sales marks them unsold. They must stay in `Review` until reconciled.
- All **325** sold records' original source sales-price and remaining-balance values agree with normalized values; **0** differences in this local comparison.
- Original buyer fields also agree with normalized fields when normalized for whitespace/case; the **18 blank buyer names** remain unresolved, not repaired.
- **10 Sold** records have a positive customer outstanding balance (not proof any amount is collectible without historical supporting documents).

The portable read-only CLI now includes aggregate counts for `originalSaleEvidenceAudit`, `crossSheetStatusConflicts` and `soldWithPositiveOutstandingBalance`, and its synthetic regression tests ensure source-sheet price/balance/buyer differences are detected without exposing the original values.

**Do not** treat these source-matching counts as proof of cloud sale/customer ID mappings, completeness of source records, paid receipts or a production import. Original records, source values, exact IDs and their review flags remain untouched.

## Strict hosted-revision and sale-mapping preflight (subsequent development)

The read-only cloud import preview now refuses a missing, malformed, duplicated or
noncanonical D1 global revision rather than interpreting absent metadata as revision 0.
Only a verified existing integer revision can be compared; no initialization or
migration occurs. Invalid original backups or corrupt cloud payloads cannot be
mistaken for a successful historical mapping.

Every historical Sold vehicle is explicitly marked as requiring verified sale ID,
customer identity, and receipts/balance reconciliation, **even if exactly one D1
sale points to the same vehicle**. Matching counts, email/name similarity and
vehicle references are not historical transaction proof; blank buyer names are
retained as blank. A preview remains advisory and not an import authorization.

## Original Excel header reconciliation fix (15 October 2026)

Read-only inspection of the preserved version-3 backup found that the original
sales workbook uses the literal header `REMAINNING AMOUNT` (double-N spelling).
The earlier audit queried `REMAINING AMOUNT` and falsely counted 325 sold rows as
balance mismatches because it failed to locate the column. The audit now accepts
both exact spellings, refuses missing/ambiguous original balance evidence and
never rewrites Excel labels or source data. These are **audit-only** changes:
no buyer, vehicle, sale or bank values are modified. Staging D1 and 386-row
sale/customer/payment ID reconciliation still require separate owner review.

## Offline legacy-versus-cloud comparison (15 October 2026)

A new **no-write**, aggregate-only comparison command is available after an
Owner has independently obtained an authentic 27-table D1 export:

```sh
node scripts/compare-local-browser-cloud.mjs /local/private/naina-browser-backup.json /local/private/verified-d1-snapshot.json
```

It verifies the cloud snapshot's canonical SHA-256, exact table list, global
revision and cross-table recovery relationships, validates the original
browser-backup structure, then compares vehicle IDs, registration/chassis
collisions, byte-equivalent canonical payloads and sold-vehicle sale ID
coverage. Reports contain counts and review flags **only**, not private names,
vehicle IDs, phone numbers or registration strings. It does not upload,
import, create ID mappings, execute SQL or mutate either source file.

A clean collision count **does not** authorize migration: real historical sale
IDs, customer identities, payment and outstanding-balance ledgers, private R2
file bytes, Owner authentication and an independently restored backup still
require verification. Every report must contain `migrationAllowed:false`.
Never put the original browser backup or exported cloud snapshot into GitHub.

## 25 October 2026 — original spreadsheet identity-evidence gate (development)

The read-only browser-backup audit now checks each vehicle's preserved
`sourceSalesRow` and original `S NO.` source cell separately. Both must be
present, positive, unambiguous, and unique after canonical numeric comparison.
Duplicate spreadsheet line numbers, duplicated serials (including `001` vs
`1`), malformed numbers and missing values are counted without printing any
business IDs or source-cell values. Synthetic regression tests cover these
fail-closed cases.

The owner's private backup was also independently examined offline: all **386**
records (including 325 Sold) have separate unique positive source-sales rows
and source serials; all 325 sold records retain their source rows. This makes
historical sale evidence traceable but **does not** establish unique D1 sale
IDs, customer identity, payment receipts or any right to import. The 18 sold
records without buyer names and 3 Review records remain unchanged.
This development adds **no** cloud writes, import switch, or source mutation.

## Projection-integrity barrier — next development batch

Before deciding that a matching D1 vehicle is identical to the browser original,
`planImport` now verifies that each existing D1 row has a valid revision and
that its projected `status`, normalized `registration_key`, and `chassis_key`
agree with its own preserved JSON payload and exact row ID. Invalid/duplicate
cloud rows block the whole preview. Differences between original source status
or vehicle identity keys and a self-consistent cloud record are conflicts, not
silent updates, even if an old per-vehicle revision matches.

The preview query now reads the D1 `status` column explicitly.
The independent checksum-verified 27-table snapshot relationship audit also
refuses mismatched registration/chassis projections, including those that would
otherwise bypass SQLite foreign-key verification. No existing source values
are inferred or rewritten. Synthetic fixtures cover false skips, tampered
projections, stale revisions and identical records.

**Release switches remain off.** This is detection and testing only, not
an import, schema migration, hosted Owner verification or production release.

{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2017",
    "lib": [
      "dom",
      "dom.iterable",
      "esnext"
    ],
    "allowJs": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "strict": true,
    "noEmit": true,
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "module": "esnext",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "resolveJsonModule": true,
    "isolatedModules": true,
    "jsx": "react-jsx",
    "incremental": true,
    "plugins": [
      {
        "name": "next"
      }
    ],
    "paths": {
      "@/*": [
        "./*"
      ]
    },
    "types": [
      "node",
      "@cloudflare/workers-types"
    ]
  },
  "include": [
    "next-env.d.ts",
    "**/*.ts",
    "**/*.tsx",
    ".next/types/**/*.ts",
    ".next/dev/types/**/*.ts",
    "**/*.mts"
  ],
  "exclude": [
    "node_modules",
    "examples"
  ]
}

docs/PRIVATE_MEDIA_RECOVERY.md.value:
# Private media recovery and independent backup

This is a development runbook. No hosted recovery or backup has been executed.
`PRIVATE_MEDIA_ENABLED` remains false. Production activation and all resource
operations require separate owner authorization. A browser JSON backup does not
contain R2 file bytes and cannot independently recover uploaded files.

## Implemented API behavior

All operations use the existing server owner guard, then the disabled-by-default
media gate, before obtaining either binding. Mutations require same-origin checks.
No API accepts caller-selected R2 keys or returns public object URLs.

For an upload, the client should generate one `uploadId` (16–100 letters, digits,
underscores or hyphens), retain it until completion, and reuse it only with the
same vehicle, filename, category, MIME and bytes. Metadata is staged before R2
writes. Exact-token retries preserve the metadata ID; changed content returns
409. Two initial concurrent requests may produce one 201 and one 503; the losing
request safely retries the same token. There is no multipart resume: retry sends
the whole file. Never generate a fresh token just because a response was lost.

`list` exposes the `incomplete` status, checksum and byte length but hides keys.
`reconcile` verifies the actual object checksum before activating an incomplete
row. Missing bytes require reupload with the original token/file; corrupted bytes
require explicit administrative review. No automatic object deletion occurs.
`archive` retains both metadata and bytes, including for sold vehicles. `restore`
unarchives only after checksum verification; it is not disaster recovery.

`preview` supports JPEG/PNG/WebP. PDF and restricted HEIC use attachment downloads;
there is no PDF renderer or HEIC conversion. Signature validation is a format
check, not malware scanning or proof that an image decoder can render the file.
File limit is the server's `MEDIA_MAX_BYTES` (15 MiB by default).

## Independent backup procedure (after approved activation)

1. Pause media mutations for a consistent snapshot. Export D1 independently,
   including all `vehicle_media` columns and associated vehicle rows. Keep the
   database export encrypted/private and separate from browser backups.
2. Paginate `list` for each vehicle, including archived rows. Save a private
   manifest containing media ID, exact vehicle ID, filename, MIME, category,
   byte length, checksum, cover and archive state. Do not expose it in web assets.
3. For each complete row, request owner-authenticated `action=export` with its
   exact vehicle/media ID. Unlike download, export includes archived objects;
   it verifies actual bytes against the recorded SHA-256. Save bytes under the
   media ID, retaining their mapping in the private manifest.
4. Independently recompute every saved file's SHA-256 and byte length. Require a
   one-to-one match between complete metadata rows and verified files. Record
   pending rows separately: a pending/missing/corrupt object is an incomplete
   backup, not a successful full backup. Retain original retry files/tokens when
   available. Keep two independent protected backup copies.
5. The current interface exports files individually. A complete automated bulk
   exporter, consistency lock and resumable backup job are not implemented.

## Disaster-restore procedure and limits

Do not restore over the live bucket or live database. Under separately approved
administrative tooling, restore the database to an isolated environment first.
Recover each verified media file at the exact opaque `object_key` from the matching
D1 export and set its `sha256` custom metadata and content type. Refuse keys absent
from the database manifest, conflicts and overwrites. Keep original media IDs,
archive state and vehicle links. No public ACL or URL should be introduced.

Before any cutover, compare all metadata IDs/counts, hash every restored object,
exercise owner-authenticated export/preview, anonymous rejection, archived-state
handling, and sold-vehicle links; test the restored database and bucket together.
Retain the previous complete pair. Do not point live code at a partly restored pair.

The API does not provide arbitrary-key restore or bucket-level cloning. Those
operations require platform-supported administrative access that has not been
verified here. Therefore end-to-end hosted disaster recovery is NOT claimed
complete. Local mock tests verify staged-upload recovery, exact-token retry,
checksum refusal, metadata archive/unarchive and archived-byte export only.

## Additional development: audited vehicle media manifest

The owner-guarded `action=manifest` GET operation now audits one vehicle's private R2 objects in pages of at most 50 records, with a stable D1 revision check. It compares R2 HEAD existence, byte length and stored SHA-256 **metadata** to each D1 media row. The output omits `object_key` and all upload-owner identifiers, and clearly marks archived, pending, missing and mismatched objects. The manifest includes neither file bytes nor a verified-content claim. HEAD verification does not replace full-blob SHA-256 verification.

When cloud/private-media gates are eventually enabled, the vehicle's Photo Gallery can download a revision-validated JSON metadata audit and its archived rows can be exported individually without first unarchiving them. The browser never saves a partial or inconsistent paginated audit, changes inventory, restores an object automatically, or stores R2 bytes in localStorage. The owner must still export every real file, compare each independent SHA-256 and keep a protected off-site backup.

The new tests cover metadata-only manifest privacy, revision races, missing/corrupt R2 headers, incomplete uploads, archived export, client pagination and malformed reports. Backend/transport code is still development-only; hosted D1/R2 tests and complete disaster recovery remain outstanding.

## Reduced metadata exposure and canonical revision gate

The generic Owner CRM feature endpoints now omit each media row's private R2
`object_key` and `uploaded_by` fields from JSON before responding; the private
media service alone retains the keys for authenticated byte operations. The
read-only recovery manifest now refuses absent or noncanonical D1 revisions,
including empty, hex, exponent, padded and unsafe integers, before checking R2.
This does not change the D1 schema, delete media, activate private routes or
remove the need for a separately verified off-site media backup.


## Offline private-media byte-backup verification (new development candidate)

After obtaining an authentic complete **27-table D1 JSON snapshot**, retain the
SHA-256 of the **exact raw JSON file** on a separate protected copy. The
snapshot's embedded SHA-256 alone is not independent evidence against someone
altering both JSON and its embedded checksum.

When the owner-authorized media export facility is separately enabled in a safe
staging/approved environment, export **every** complete private file, including
archived photos/documents, and save each in a private local directory under
the opaque media ID + \`.bin\`. Example: an exported D1 media row with
\`id: "sample-file-1"\` becomes \`private-media/sample-file-1.bin\`.
**Do not use the R2 object key or original filename** for local paths. Do not
save files in GitHub, the showroom website or a public share.

On Windows PowerShell, independently fingerprint the original export file:

\`\`\`powershell
(Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 ".\private-d1-snapshot.json").Hash.ToLowerInvariant()
\`\`\`

Retain that exact digest separately (offline and protected). Then run the
**read-only** verifier after fetching a separate, unchanged copy of that export:

\`\`\`sh
node scripts/verify-private-media-backup.mjs private-d1-snapshot.json private-media YOUR_PREVIOUSLY_RECORDED_64_CHARACTER_SHA256
\`\`\`

Or run the same command with \`pnpm run audit:media-backup --\` prefixed.

This tool refuses an incorrect independent raw-file checksum, invalid internal
canonical checksum, schema/revision/relationship inconsistencies, unsafe media
IDs or symlinks, missing/extra media files, modified/shortened file bytes, and
unresolved pending uploads. Each archived object is required exactly once.
It streams SHA-256 over the **actual local saved bytes** and compares their
length/hash to \`vehicle_media\` in the D1 snapshot. It prints only aggregate
counts and no file names, private IDs or customer/registration data. A nonzero
exit code means the copy is incomplete or untrusted. This tool never uploads,
mutates, restores or enables any source system.

Passing this tool verifies **one local copy only**. It does not prove
independent offsite retention, real hosted R2 restore, staging Owner
authentication, a consistent production D1/R2 export, or production approval.
Those are separate and still pending. In particular it cannot export or
download objects from an account it is not connected to.


**Checkout privacy guard:** The repo now excludes `private-media/` and named
`private-d1-snapshot*.json` / `verified-d1-snapshot*.json` paths from Git.
Keep **all** real backups outside the checkout anyway; ignore rules are only a
secondary guard and cannot protect a file already tracked or manually forced.

docs/PRIVATE_HISTORICAL_SALE_REVIEW.md.value:
# Private historical sale reconciliation — offline review only

This is for the Naina Motors private Dealer Desk CRM. Do **not** send original
backups, exported review worksheets, sales/customer evidence or bank records to
GitHub. Do not run on the showroom repository. No production data is mutated.

The historical version-3 browser backup contains 386 vehicle records, including
325 Sold and three Review statuses. Some original Sold rows have no buyer name.
The CRM must preserve these omissions; neither a workbook serial number nor a
sale-sheet line number is a verified D1 `sales.id` or customer/payment identity.

## Build the owner-private review worksheet (on the owner's computer)

From the Dealer Desk code checkout, with Node.js 22+:

```sh
node scripts/create-private-sale-review.mjs /absolute/path/to/original-browser-backup.json /absolute/path/outside/repository/naina-historical-sale-review.json
```

On Windows, supply fully qualified drive paths, for example
`C:\Private\original-browser-backup.json` and
`C:\Private\naina-historical-sale-review.json`.

The script only reads the original backup and creates one **new** JSON review
worksheet outside the source repository. It refuses input backups located inside the source repository, relative output paths,
output within the GitHub repository, overwrite/re-run on an existing output
file, invalid backups or missing source evidence structure. Unix output file
permissions are set to 0600; on Windows secure the enclosing private directory
with appropriate NTFS permissions. No cookies, keys or network credentials.
The console prints only counts and the source SHA-256.

The worksheet contains confidential registration, chassis, buyer and sale
evidence; **never attach it to a PR, issue, CI artifact or public page**.
It includes all Sold and Review records in original order, with unchanged
source identifiers and source-sheet references. Available records are counted
but not invented as historical sales. No new sale IDs, buyer names, customer
IDs, payments, reconciled balances or import decisions are generated.

## Required next gates

1. Verify Owner-only staging identity and a genuine D1 snapshot separately.
2. Compare the original source with the verified target snapshot and document
   actual historical sale/customer identities and any payment proof.
3. Have the Owner resolve three Review status conflicts and review the 18
   missing buyer names without inventing data. An unresolved blank can remain.
4. Back up and restore both D1 rows and R2 media bytes independently.
5. Implement a separately gated, transaction-checked import plan only after
   identity, balance and record conflicts have been reviewed.

A generated worksheet is a **starting point for human reconciliation**, not a
cloud migration, a recovery backup, or authorization to modify the CRM.

## Optional authenticated-cloud candidate comparison (private, offline)

After obtaining a genuine **complete 27-table D1 export** and an independently
recorded SHA-256 of the **raw** cloud JSON file, pass both to the same local
review command:

```sh
node scripts/create-private-sale-review.mjs /absolute/original-browser-backup.json /absolute/new-private-review.json /absolute/verified-cloud-snapshot.json INDEPENDENT_RAW_SNAPSHOT_SHA256
```

Both private inputs and the new output must remain outside the GitHub checkout.
The command verifies the independently supplied raw cloud SHA-256, the
snapshot's internal canonical SHA-256 and the full cross-table relationship
audit before writing a review. An invalid/reused target, inconsistent snapshot,
or existing output file aborts without overwriting any source.

A matching cloud `vehicle_id` yields **candidate** existing sale IDs, linked
customer IDs and counts of existing payment rows for owner investigation.
Neither a matching ID nor a payment-row count proves original customer identity,
historical receipt amounts or balances. Cloud status differences remain
conflicts. The private output preserves missing buyer fields and Review statuses,
leaves all mapping decisions PENDING, and is **always import-disabled**.

Console output contains aggregate counts only. Never commit or share either
the snapshot or enriched private worksheet; a passing report does not prove
hosted login, storage isolation or disaster recovery.

cloud-preparation/README.md.value:
# Cloud integration preparation

Version 15 remains the separately saved/deployed storage-free recovery baseline at commit 6235df3bd9ebc0b4a1fd03d5a043e7477a25544f.

For this UNPUBLISHED candidate the five original migration files have been moved back to root `drizzle/`, byte-for-byte, and the generator output restored to `./drizzle`. The unchanged 27-table schema remains in `db/schema.ts`. The candidate manifest declares future DB and BUCKET bindings; all operation gates remain false.

This candidate is NOT a migration-free UI release. A future deployment requests provisioning/connection of D1 and private R2 and hosted schema migrations before Worker upload. Saving this candidate does not execute that deployment. Never deploy it under the prior Version 15 UI-only authorization.

See `docs/CLOUD_CANDIDATE.md` and `docs/PRIVATE_MEDIA_RECOVERY.md` for capability limits, testing, recovery, and required separate approvals. Historical SQL, snapshots and journal entries must not be rewritten.

docs/CLOUD_RESTORE_RELATIONSHIP_AUDIT.md.value:
# Cloud snapshot relationship audit — development only

This applies solely to the PRIVATE Naina Motors Dealer Desk GitHub branch. Production cloud transfer remains disabled, and the customer showroom is completely separate.

## Purpose
A SHA-256 checksum confirms that the JSON snapshot has not changed since export. It **does not** establish that sales point to existing vehicles, customer payments point to existing sales, or original vehicle IDs, stock statuses and attached-file links are mutually consistent.

A new gated owner-only read-only action is prepared:

`POST /api/private-crm-transfer`
`{"action":"audit","snapshot":{...the exported snapshot...}}`

**The route first calls `verifySnapshot`**, which checks the exact 27-table manifest, the supplied SHA-256, bounded rows and format. Only after those checks succeed does it run `auditSnapshotLinks`. It returns the original verification and a bounded integrity report. This action never accesses a D1 database, writes records, performs migration, restores R2 objects, or changes the browser's `naina-desk-v1` storage key.

## Checks
- Duplicated/missing primary IDs, including composite-key feature tables.
- Foreign links from sales, expenses, vehicle documents/media, location, RTO, inspections, reservations, reminders, and payments.
- More than one sale linked to a vehicle, sold stock without a unique sale, available stock with a sale.
- Status and original ID disagreements between a vehicle's D1 row and its preserved JSON payload.
- Duplicate parking/other total rows, malformed monetary amounts, invalid payment amounts.
- Media metadata presence, byte count, version and recorded SHA-256 format; duplicate R2 object keys, invalid/duplicate active cover flags, and incomplete upload rows. The audit **does not** read or verify actual R2 file bytes.

The report contains `checkedTables`, `checkedRows`, `issueCount`, bounded issue codes and exact IDs needed for reconciliation, and `consistent`. It is marked `readOnly:true` and `mediaBytesVerified:false`. If errors exceed the report limit, `truncated:true` means there are more issues to resolve. Raw customer/vehicle payloads and R2 storage keys are not returned.

## Preconditions and remaining work
1. Obtain a genuine owner-authenticated, checksum-verifiable D1 snapshot with every expected table. Never treat a browser inventory JSON backup as an equivalent 27-table cloud snapshot.
2. Run checksum verification and relational audit. Resolve errors before planning any cloud cutover. Keep unmodified original backup separately.
3. Rehearse restore with `node scripts/verify-cloud-restore.mjs SNAPSHOT.json` against disposable SQLite. This runs structural foreign-key, integrity and record round-trip tests; it never writes to production.
4. Separately export every R2 object and validate its full bytes and SHA-256; this audit cannot restore or verify R2 file contents.
5. Complete production build, hosted owner-auth D1/R2 tests, mobile tests, offsite backup verification, transaction reconciliation and an approved, reversible cutover.

The production flags `CLOUD_TRANSFER_ENABLED`, `MAIN_CRM_CLOUD_PREVIEW_ENABLED`, `CRM_WRITES_ENABLED` and `PRIVATE_MEDIA_ENABLED` stay **false**. **No import executor or production restore mechanism is enabled by this batch.**

## Stronger offline restore gate

The disposable offline restore runner now checksum-verifies the source, then
applies the bounded relationship audit before SQLite schema/foreign-key and exact
row round-trip verification. This catches logically inconsistent but SQL-valid
snapshots, such as Sold inventory lacking a sale. A failing audit prints only the
issue count and a generic failure, not vehicle/customer IDs. This still does not
verify private R2 bytes, create an off-site backup, or authorize a deployment.

## Revision and client-side reconciliation safeguards

Snapshots with a missing/noncanonical global cloud revision are no longer
considered recoverable. The cloud dashboard additionally refuses Sold vehicles
without linked sale rows and refuses normalized receipt totals that, together
with the recorded outstanding balance, exceed the selling price. Historical
payments may be incomplete, so the client does **not** infer that a lower sum
proves complete financial reconciliation.

## Cross-device monotonicity and snapshot input validation

The optional cloud revision watcher now rejects an older server revision,
invalidates in-flight polls after manually acknowledged refreshes and does not
accept an applied revision older than the one that prompted the refresh. This
prevents revision counters from silently moving backwards on a laptop/iPhone.
Snapshot verification now validates the SHA-256 hex form and excludes nonfinite
numeric values before restore checks. Neither safeguard activates cloud mode,
reads browser backups or performs any hosted write.

## Financial mirrors in recovery snapshots

The read-only relationship audit now compares sale price and remaining balance
between linked `sales.payload_json` and `vehicles.payload_json` when both values
are present, checks parking/other/combined vehicle costs, and matches recorded
expense rows against their vehicle totals. It also blocks recorded receipts
plus outstanding balance from exceeding selling price. Lower receipt totals
are not proof of missing payments, so historic gaps are never filled by guesses.
A discrepancy blocks the disposable restore rehearsal without altering any
source file or exposing names, amounts or R2 object keys in error output.

The existing browser dashboard now checks the complete cloud snapshot revision
against both the revision previously displayed and the revision reported by a
poll, **before** replacing in-memory vehicle state. If a replica returns older
data, it retains the current view and flags the refresh as unsuccessful;
`naina-desk-v1` and the original backup remain untouched.

The browser cloud projector also fails closed if a vehicle location is duplicated
or linked to missing inventory, a document/media row references an unknown
vehicle, or a general cloud-media response includes a private R2 storage key or
upload-owner ID. Such records must be repaired, not silently dropped from the
Owner dashboard. The server-side generic media feed is separately redacted.

## Additional pre-restore identity integrity (development-only)

The 27-table relational audit now also refuses any D1 sale whose embedded
historical `customerId` disagrees with its projected `customer_id` link.
Missing optional historic buyer/customer fields are not fabricated, and a
legitimately absent payload link is not treated as proof of a specific buyer.

Vehicle snapshots now reject invalid status labels, duplicate normalized
real registration/chassis keys and non-canonical indexed projections, including
a placeholder stored as a claimed registration. `UNREG`, `N/A` and similar
placeholders must remain NULL in the indexed D1 projection while preserving
their original source literal inside `payload_json`.

All checks are read-only and synthetic test coverage verifies they block a
signed but semantically inconsistent export. A green result still does not
prove a genuine hosted Owner login or successful hosted database/media restore.


## Independent raw fingerprint required for offline SQLite verification

The exact, previously recorded lowercase SHA-256 of the **raw private snapshot
JSON file bytes** is now mandatory for \`verify-cloud-restore.mjs\`:

\`\`\`sh
node scripts/verify-cloud-restore.mjs /absolute/private/snapshot.json PREVIOUSLY_RECORDED_RAW_SHA256
\`\`\`

The command rejects symlinked exports, relative paths or backups under the
GitHub checkout. It never exposes input file paths in failure output and cannot
alter the original export. The embedded snapshot hash alone is not sufficient
to prove an unmodified earlier export. The recommended one-command paired
readiness runner in \`docs/PRIVATE_RECOVERY_PAIR.md\` automatically performs
this SQLite check on both independent copies using their already supplied
fingerprints. Both are **offline-only**, not hosted disaster recovery.

EXPORT-README.md.value:
# Version 16 source export

Project: appgprj_6aca62581e288191af74309f0392facc
Saved version: appgprj_6aca62581e288191af74309f0392facc~appgver_851a05eee3e88191a15bc1553cc90d7d
Source commit: 35e425627f0662f41000349a7b2e4feebce0166e

All 168 included tracked files are byte-identical to this commit. EXPORT-README.md and EXPORT-MANIFEST.json are export-only additions. No Site source was changed.

## Included and excluded
Includes frontend, backend, API routes, reusable components, configuration, dependency manifests/lockfile, test fixtures, documentation, private R2 service code and all five preserved Drizzle SQL/journal/snapshot files (27-table schema). The build/ directory contains required build plugin SOURCE, not generated output; keep it.

Excluded tracked file: source-data/imported-data.js (private business inventory dataset). No replacement dataset was fabricated. Dependencies, compiled builds, Git history, environment secrets, runtime caches, browser backups and production database/media contents are not included. The owner email allowlist is retained as non-secret authorization configuration; it is not a login credential.

## Develop locally
Use Node >=22.13 (Node 24 used for verification), pnpm 11.25.0, Python 3 with sqlite3 and a `python` command pointing to Python 3. Linux/macOS shell or WSL is recommended.

1. Install pnpm 11.25.0 and run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`.
2. Run `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`.
3. Run `pnpm dev` for local development or `pnpm build` for a production build.
4. Run independent tests with:
   `node --test $(find tests -name '*.test.mjs' ! -name 'release-safety.test.mjs')`
5. Run `python tests/schema-additions.test.py`. Nine standalone checks run without Git history; the one historical comparison described below cannot pass in this export.

`tests/release-safety.test.mjs` has two historical comparisons requiring Git history; its inventory preservation test also needs the intentionally excluded private dataset. `tests/schema-additions.test.py::test_03_original_history_immutable` and `scripts/verify-cloud-candidate.py` require historical Git commits. These provenance checks cannot fully run from a history-free export. No excluded data or history is needed for application compilation or the other synthetic service tests. EXPORT-MANIFEST.json provides per-file SHA-256 checksums for this export instead.

## Hosting dependencies and limitations
This is complete development source, not a portable hosted account. Sites authentication uses trusted platform-injected identity headers and Sites sign-in routes; an unrelated host must implement secure authentication and trusted ingress before serving private routes. Never trust identity headers sent directly by a browser. Sites access policy, custom-domain ownership, deployment records and credentials are not transferable code.

D1/R2 services target Cloudflare Worker bindings DB and BUCKET. Local services are tested using disposable SQLite and mocked R2. Real bindings, account resources and media are not exported. The .openai/hosting.json binding declarations and build plugin are preserved, but provisioning a different hosting target requires its own configuration and authorization.

All five cloud release gates remain false. Do not enable them just to make local tests pass. Original CRM uses browser-local naina-desk-v1 records; the separate cloud workspace never automatically imports or overwrites them. No actual business import/cutover or complete media disaster restore exists yet. See docs/CLOUD_CANDIDATE.md and docs/PRIVATE_MEDIA_RECOVERY.md for current scope and activation blockers. Root README.md is preserved historical documentation and describes an older stage; prefer these newer documents.

No fresh dependency download or alternative-host deployment was performed for this export. Export-copy tests use the existing installed dependency versions. Production and the separate showroom were untouched.

## Export verification
164 JavaScript tests and 9 history-independent schema checks passed from the exported copy, as did full-project TypeScript checking. The saved source previously passed its production build and full 169 JavaScript + 10 schema suite. All 168 exported source files were compared byte-for-byte against the exact commit. ZIP integrity and required-file checks passed.

docs/HOSTED_CLOUD_SECURITY_GATE.md.value:
# Naina Motors Dealer Desk — Hosted Owner/D1/R2 preflight

This is for the PRIVATE Dealer Desk only. The customer showroom repository must not be modified.

## Implemented read-only diagnostic (development branch)

`GET /api/private-crm-preflight` requires the existing server-trusted Sites Owner identity **before** evaluating its independent server-only feature flag. `HOSTED_READONLY_PREFLIGHT_ENABLED: boolean = false` by default. An authorized request receives **423 Locked** while the flag is off; unauthenticated/nonowner requests are denied before any database or bucket access. There is no browser or query-string override.

If this route is deliberately enabled on a **disposable staging deployment**, it does nothing but:

1. Use the platform D1 `DB` binding to read the SQLite table/index names and definitions, compare with the expected 27-table schema, require all six critical indexes to be **UNIQUE** (names alone are insufficient), require a canonical nonnegative safe-decimal `cloud_metadata.revision`, and run `PRAGMA foreign_key_check`. This is still not a full constraint, column-shape or migration-history proof.
2. Call `BUCKET.list({limit:1})` on the private R2 binding. It does **not** download an object or return its key, content, URL, size, user or media metadata.
3. Return a `no-store`, `nosniff` JSON infrastructure report: missing schema/index identifiers, revision validity, foreign-key-violation count, R2 binding success and `infrastructureReady`. It returns no vehicle rows, customer identities, sales figures, storage keys or secrets.

The response deliberately says `migrationExecuted:false`, `mediaBytesVerified:false`, `liveReleaseApproved:false`. A successful read-only probe does NOT authorize D1 writes, enable any cloud editing, prove login ingress cannot be bypassed, or establish backup/restore readiness.

## Separate hosted security checks still required

- From an **unauthenticated** browser, confirm all `/api/private-crm-main`, `/api/private-crm-write`, `/api/private-crm-transfer`, `/api/private-media`, and `/api/private-crm-preflight` paths deny access **before** D1/R2 connection. Verify neither private metadata nor protected data is returned.
- With an authenticated **nonowner** account, repeat and confirm 403 for protected routes. Never pass user identity via caller-supplied headers or query values. Confirm the actual Sites ingress strips/replaces any spoofed `oai-authenticated-user-*` headers; verify there is no public direct Worker bypass.
- With the real verified Site owner on staging, confirm only the read-only diagnostic is activated. All CRM writes, media uploads, cloud transfer and live deployment remain locked. Confirm the Site-scoped Owner subject before relying on subject-based identity authorization; the repository currently has `OWNER_SUBJECT = null` and an email policy fallback.
- Provision and test disposable D1 and R2 bindings. Confirm 27 tables, required indexes, revision, no foreign-key violations and R2 read access. The debug report must not contain any R2 object key, authenticated ID or customer/vehicle data.
- Independently confirm that unauthenticated HTTP responses have no-store/nosniff and no permissive CORS for private resources. Do not record live tokens, cookies, customer IDs or private file URLs in CI logs.
- Keep existing `naina-desk-v1` browser records and verified JSON backups untouched. No automated startup migration; no real 386-record import until preview/ID reconciliation and restore rehearsals succeed.

## Developer verification

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
node --test tests/hosted-readonly-preflight.test.mjs
pnpm run preflight:source
pnpm exec tsc --noEmit
pnpm exec vinext build
```

These are synthetic tests and a local build, **not hosted verification**. The isolated built-Worker smoke now checks eight private GET routes, denial headers (no-store/nosniff/no permissive CORS), and a cross-origin write rejection. The GitHub Actions workflow runs them without any production Firebase/Sites/Cloudflare secrets or deployment permissions.

**Release decision:** HOLD until real private hosted Owner authentication, D1/R2 access, backup, migration and iPhone reconciliation are verified. Leave `HOSTED_READONLY_PREFLIGHT_ENABLED` and every other server release flag at `false` on `main` and production. No new production deployment was performed in this development batch.

## Transaction revision hardening (development only)

The two write services now require an already initialised, canonical safe-integer
`cloud_metadata.revision` row. They never silently create revision zero, coerce
malformed revision text or advance an invalid revision. D1 batch assertions
provide an atomic revision comparison for both CRM and private-media changes.
This is a source-code and synthetic-test safeguard; a deliberate, audited
initialisation on disposable staging is required before any positive write test.
**Do not seed or modify production D1 through this development change.**

## Simulated two-device convergence (development only)

`tests/two-device-cloud-convergence.test.mjs` drives two independent cloud
preview readers and revision watchers against one fictional in-memory server.
It verifies refresh, edit deferral, convergence and stale-revision rejection,
without localStorage, data migration, network access or real business records.
This is **not** a physical iPhone/laptop test or proof of hosted consistency.
Both must still be tested with actual private staging accounts and D1/R2.

## Legacy status read consistency

The legacy Owner cloud-status route now reports `revision:null` and
`revisionValid:false` for missing, padded, nondecimal, or out-of-range global
revisions, rather than fabricating revision zero. This read-only improvement
does not enable the legacy cloud feature, seed any metadata row, import data or
modify hosted databases. Disposable synthetic regression tests cover both valid
and malformed metadata.

## Precise unique-index contract checks

The offline and staged hosted read-only schema checks now verify eight critical
UNIQUE indexes, including active-reservation and document-expiry uniqueness.
The actual indexed table, ordered columns and any partial WHERE predicate must
match the expected schema. A same-named index on the wrong columns is a release
blocker even if it is UNIQUE. This work cannot apply migrations or activate
production cloud switches.

## No-write staging verification command (latest development addition)

For an explicitly marked disposable **staging** hostname only:

```sh
node scripts/verify-hosted-staging.mjs --origin https://staging.crm.nainamotors.com
```

This CLI deliberately **rejects production** `crm.nainamotors.com` and showroom URLs.
It makes seven unauthenticated **GET** requests without cookies, automatic redirects
or response-body reads. It checks 401/403 denial, no-store/nosniff and no CORS
for every private route. On a dedicated `staging.crm.nainamotors.com`
(or `sandbox.crm.nainamotors.com` / `preview.crm.nainamotors.com`) hostname,
it also performs seven **read-only forged identity-header GETs** with the
configured Owner email and a fictional caller ID. Those must still return
401/403. A 423 lock response to a forged identity is a **security failure**:
the request passed the Owner guard despite the absence of a real login.
The Owner email is never sent to arbitrary third-party staging domains. These
checks never read response bodies, seed D1, test genuine Owner login, read R2
objects, run SQL or submit POST requests. A passing result does not prove
all direct Worker origins are unreachable; that needs separate hosted review.

A verified Owner may later save the **sanitized JSON** from the independent
read-only staging diagnostic, without including cookies, tokens or business
records, then review it offline:

```sh
node scripts/verify-hosted-staging.mjs --report private-staging-preflight.json
```

That only checks the report's internal structure and claimed readiness.
It is NOT independent proof of the Owner's ingress identity, positive D1
writes, blob SHA-256, complete backup, data migration or launch approval.

Never run these commands against production or use a green report to enable
release switches. This code is development-only until real staging exists.

## Ephemeral Cloudflare-compatible D1/R2 integration (development only)

The isolated `node scripts/test-local-cloud-bindings.mjs` runner constructs a
throwaway Wrangler configuration under the OS temporary directory with fake
binding identifiers, executes both SQL migration files using `--local` and
`--persist-to`, and runs a **local Worker** on 127.0.0.1. This test exercises
the actual local runtime bindings: 27 tables, synthetic vehicle insert/read,
UNIQUE registration constraint, foreign-key rejection, synthetic R2 object
put/get/list/delete, and byte-for-byte SHA-256 verification. It refuses
`--remote` or `--preview` flags, strips account credentials, and deletes
all temporary local state afterward. CI runs it after the existing built
Worker security smoke. No production records or passwords are used.

This remains a LOCAL simulator check, **not hosted D1/R2 or Sites Owner
verification**; it does not change source flags, deploy anything, perform
real backup restoration or authorize a cloud release.

# Step 26 — main dashboard cloud preview (development only)

This branch **does not activate cloud mode**. The main-dashboard API is guarded by `MAIN_CRM_CLOUD_PREVIEW_ENABLED=false` in `lib/main-crm-flags.ts`. Existing D1/R2 read, write, import and upload release gates remain disabled.

The original dashboard still starts with browser-local records and makes **zero cloud requests on startup**. An explicit **View cloud data** button requests owner-only paginated D1 rows, validates all pages against a stable global revision and checks record identity/status/sale conflicts. Any incomplete, denied or conflicting response leaves local records untouched. Complete results replace only the in-memory view, marked **Cloud preview · read-only**. Manual refresh reads again. **Return to browser data** rereads the unchanged `naina-desk-v1` key.

During preview the local save, restore, forms and browser-backup controls reject mutation. The existing separate cloud editing workspace remains the only prepared edit interface. D1 document requirements are shown separately from original Excel document flags. Media metadata is projected but private file bytes are not downloaded by the main gallery.

**Not complete:** migration/cutover, direct main-form D1 writes, live D1/R2 provisioning, hosted/iPhone verification, automated cross-device sync, offline queue, full financial reconciliation, media restore and disaster recovery. Do not claim these are implemented or deploy this branch. Production activation needs fresh owner backup, reconciliation, full tests, explicit separate owner approvals and hosted identity/storage security verification.

## Second development batch — no deployment
- The new edit controls require `MAIN_CRM_CLOUD_PREVIEW_ENABLED` **and** `CRM_WRITES_ENABLED` on the SERVER; default values remain false. The owner must separately approve D1 migrations, backup verification, cloud import, hosted testing and both gates before real business writes.
- Location and document status forms call the existing private write endpoint; the owner guard enforces same-origin mutations. The server sets changed/updated timestamps for those two resources.
- An ambiguous save result must be refreshed and reconciled before trying again; never treat a timeout as a failed transaction and replay with a new token.
- This remains a development-only PR, not production-ready sync. Cloud R2 media, full dashboard CRUD, automated cross-device polling and off-platform recovery remain incomplete.

## Third development batch — cloud financial transactions (no production activation)

- The original vehicle finance panel can prepare cloud-only `sales`, `customer_payments`, and `expenses` updates, only when **both** server-side read and write release gates explicitly permit cloud editing. Both remain **false**.
- The read-only snapshot includes the D1 sales and expense rows, linked by **exact original IDs**. A missing, duplicate or conflicting link stops the transaction.
- Sale creation requires Available stock, unique sale linkage, buyer/date, price and outstanding balance. The existing atomic write service handles initial receipts.
- Customer payment entry is append-only, bound to exactly one reconciled original sale ID, and checked against the recorded vehicle balance. The existing atomic write service updates both sale and vehicle balances and creates the cashbook receipt; never subtract payment twice in dashboards.
- Parking/other expense edits **replace the stored total**, not create an additional expense. Duplicate or disagreeing total rows require reconciliation before editing.
- Each save requires explicit confirmation, a known cloud revision, an idempotency token, and a matching server receipt. Network-unknown outcomes must be refreshed and reconciled, not blindly retried.
- These edits do **not** auto-switch or mutate `naina-desk-v1`. Cloud D1/R2, migration/import, private photos, hosted login and iPhone tests remain unverified and unactivated.

## Audit hardening: cloud modal isolation (development branch)
- Fixed document editor helper shadowing the browser DOM document (this previously prevented the edit dialog from opening).
- Both feature and finance dialogs now require a live `canSubmit` capability at submit time and immediately before starting the write. Opening a dialog does not grant a permanent permission.
- The main dashboard increments a cloud-view epoch on every cloud refresh and on returning to browser-local mode. An older open dialog cannot submit after a mode switch or refresh, even if D1 revision remains numerically unchanged.
- New DOM-level synthetic regression tests cover dialog opening and fail-closed stale-session behavior. No production database or device tests have run.

## Fourth development batch — guarded cross-device revision checks
- New `public/main-cloud-sync.js` periodically checks the owner-guarded D1 **revision endpoint**, every 45 seconds and when the authorized browser tab regains focus. It **never starts in default browser-local mode**; the owner must deliberately enter cloud preview after the future approved migration.
- When the remote revision differs, the watcher refreshes the entire validated D1 snapshot only if no browser, document or finance editing dialog is open or saving. Otherwise it displays an **updates available** message and waits for a safe refresh. It does not discard unsaved edits or write to localStorage.
- Every completed reload validates pages and revision consistency; only then is the in-memory dashboard replaced. Failures leave the current view untouched and show a retry message. Returning to browser-local mode cancels the watcher and restores the untouched local snapshot.
- Synthetic runtime checks and new `tests/main-cloud-sync.test.mjs` cover startup gating, remote revision, safe refresh, open-edit protection, source verification and stopping during in-flight checks.
- **Not live / not enabled:** Both server-side cloud release switches are still false. No production synchronization, D1/R2 provisioning, migration or mobile verification occurred. Full production-build validation is outstanding.

## Fifth development batch — owner cloud contacts and enquiry pipeline
- Adds owner-only D1 `customers` to the existing revision-validated, paginated main CRM snapshot. Cloud contacts are shown in the existing Customers screen as a clearly separate register; the historical sold-buyer list remains unchanged.
- Prepares cloud enquiry create/edit in the existing enquiry board, without allowing the original local-only enquiry edit flow to write to browser storage while in cloud mode.
- Uses the existing private D1 write service with exact existing IDs on updates, cryptographic IDs for new leads/customers, field/date/budget validation, explicit confirmation, expected global revision, idempotency token, and verified receipt.
- Every contact dialog revalidates the active cloud mode and view epoch before submission; any open dialog prevents background refresh or exit. No retry if the outcome is unknown.
- Synthetic tests include new and existing customer/lead operations, disabled gate, untrusted response, stale dialogs, and invalid/duplicate records.
- Production `MAIN_CRM_CLOUD_PREVIEW_ENABLED` and `CRM_WRITES_ENABLED` switches are **still false**; no source data, production Sites version, D1/R2 or customer showroom changes.

## Sixth development batch — private media in main vehicle gallery
- Adds a server-declared `mediaEnabled` capability based on existing `PRIVATE_MEDIA_ENABLED=false`. The revised main-cloud adapter requires that capability to remain consistent throughout a complete revision-validated snapshot. No local default UI can enable it.
- When owner-only cloud preview and private-media authorization are active, main vehicle galleries support **private** photo/document uploads, raster previews, downloads, cover selection and archiving, including for sold bikes. All requests use existing `/api/private-media` with same-origin credentials. No public R2 URL or stored browser-local file bytes.
- Validates supported formats and 15 MiB limits, explicitly confirms uploads/changes, and refuses automatic retries after uncertain results. Re-selecting an identical file in the same tab reuses a stable in-memory upload token for the server's idempotent/reconciliation flow; server validates file hash and metadata.
- Cloud file actions remain entirely distinct from the old browser-only temporary selection UI and never write the browser's `naina-desk-v1` inventory key.
- Incomplete hosted D1/R2 activation, export/restore, malware screening, PDF/HEIC inline rendering, file-category reclassification and actual iPhone verification are **not** claimed complete.
- **All production media/database switches remain OFF.** Media UI is development-only in this draft PR; no real files were uploaded.

## Seventh development batch — atomic media revision synchronization
- Private R2 media mutations that make metadata visible (completed/reconciled upload, cover, archive, restore) now use a single **Cloudflare D1 batch** to update their metadata and increment `cloud_metadata.revision` together. An incomplete object stage does not trigger a misleading revision.
- The normal cloud watcher can therefore notice media metadata changes made on another device after cloud mode and R2 have been separately enabled. The main gallery does not retain file bytes in browser storage.
- Tested against a disposable local R2/D1 harness: **31 private-media service tests passed**, including the new revision check. Real hosted concurrency, transfer failures, iPhone Safari and production backup/restore remain unverified.
- **No production release switches were changed.**

## Eighth development batch — inventory editing and price history
- Adds guarded, explicitly confirmed D1 inventory creation and editing to the **existing Inventory screen**. Existing record updates preserve exact original IDs; new records receive unpredictable IDs. Only Available/Review can be created directly. Selling and corrections to sold status remain confined to dedicated sale/reconciliation flows.
- Direct changes to asking price are not allowed in generic vehicle updates; a separate owner-confirmed price-history form calls `price_history` to preserve old and new values with an audit reason and global revision validation.
- Validates year, purchase date, money precision, required model, stale view session and owner release gates. Failed/ambiguous writes never silently write browser-local records or auto-retry.
- Added synthetic tests for new/edit/price plan, exact ID preservation, rejection of invalid fields, verified write receipt, and stale edit dialog.
- The main cloud view, writes and private media switches remain OFF in production. No actual business records or live Sites version were changed.

## Cloud reminder task editor (development only)
The existing Reminders screen now includes Owner-gated create/edit controls
for independent reminders, including status, priority, due date and notes.
Updates preserve exact IDs and linked vehicle/lead metadata, and preserve an
existing timed due date when the calendar day is unchanged. Browser-local
records, enquiries, RTO tasks and expiry records remain distinct; no messages
or notifications are scheduled. Cloud writes and production deployment remain
OFF until hosted verification and separate release approval.

## Gated vehicle reservations, booking lifecycle and accounting isolation

In the private Main CRM, the Buyer & sale vehicle-details panel now displays
cloud reservation history and, only under the server-approved edit capability,
offers explicit creation/closure of an Active hold. Existing D1 migration
enforces one Active reservation per vehicle; read-time projection also checks
that an Active hold is on Available stock and cannot have duplicate Active rows.
An Active hold blocks creating a sale until it is separately closed as
Cancelled, Expired or Converted. Closed holds cannot be reopened through the
generic write service. This is important because reservation tokens are
**informational only** and are not booked as sale payments or cashbook receipts.
The actual sale and token reconciliation require a separate Owner-confirmed
accounting action. Neither booking nor closure silently marks a bike Sold.

The reservation UI, backend checks and tests are still behind all existing
disabled feature gates. No real D1 or R2, production write, Sites deployment,
import or live customer record has been changed.

## Independent inspection and auction history in main vehicle details

D1 `vehicle_inspections` and `auction_plans` histories now appear in their
own vehicle panels when Owner cloud mode is explicitly selected. The protected
server route validates the same global revision, page limits and authentication
as inventory. The browser checks exact vehicle links, duplicate IDs, inspection
dates and auction state/amount integrity, refusing inconsistent projections.

Owner-confirmed, new-only forms use the existing server's `CrmWrites`
service, cryptographically random record IDs, idempotency keys, strict amount
validation and known revision preconditions. Historical inspections or plans
cannot be silently replaced through these forms. Repair estimates and bid
plans are NOT real vehicle expenses, purchased bids, sales or cashbook entries.
No localStorage writes or retries after uncertain network results occur.

Production read/write/media/import release gates remain disabled. This is
unpublished development, not hosted security, mobile device, D1 migration or
recovery proof.

## Additional server-side projection and historical sale read safeguards

The private `CrmReads` service now refuses a D1 vehicle row if its stored
status, registration key or chassis projection disagrees with its own original
payload. Invalid per-row revisions are rejected before mapping. Sales rows also
must preserve exact `vehicle_id`, optional `customer_id` and valid revision,
and any explicitly stored payload links must agree with the columns. Older
historical sales that legitimately omit an optional payload link remain readable:
missing buyer/customer evidence is **not invented**.

This is a *server-side* safety boundary, before data reaches the existing
client dashboard. Source data is read-only, no original IDs change and no
import/write/media flags are enabled. New synthetic negative tests verify
bad projections are rejected without logging private values.

## Unregistered vehicle safety for cloud inventory writers

New inventory records with original placeholder registration values
`UNREG`, `UNREGISTERED`, `NA`, `N/A` and `NONE` now store a **NULL
registration projection**, not a fake indexed registration value. The original
text remains unchanged in `payload_json`. Multiple unregistered bikes may
therefore exist without colliding on an invented registration key; real
registrations and chassis keys remain uniquely protected by D1 indexes.

This corrects prospective cloud writer behavior only. Existing cloud rows
(if any) are **not automatically repaired**: historical source vs genuine
hosted D1 reconciliation is still required before data migration.

## Gated RTO/HPA and workshop repair editors in main vehicle details

The existing vehicle Work tab now exposes RTO cases and workshop jobs with
read-only original history, plus optional Owner-only cloud creation and narrow
status/follow-up updates using the existing authenticated `CrmWrites` endpoint.
History rows preserve exact arbitrary ID strings, original associated vehicle,
case procedure/reference, bank NOC/applied dates, workshop description,
estimate and original started date. Same-day timed follow-ups are not
rewritten as date-only values; historical numeric text is not reformatted
merely to change a status. Blank updates do not clear original dates.

Repairs' estimated/final costs do **not** flow automatically into
`expenses`, `vehicles.landedTotal`, purchase cost or the cashbook. RTO stage
updates cannot change the underlying original Excel/document checklist or
buyer handover. Server global revision and ownership release flags remain
mandatory; browser forms require current epoch, explicit confirmation and
exact save receipts. Unknown save results are never retried automatically.

All five release gates remain disabled. No real hosted D1, original business
record, public website or browser-local snapshot has been changed.


## Historical ID and sparse inventory-edit safeguards (unpublished)

Cloud inventory, customer/enquiry and inspection/auction form planners now
preserve whitespace-significant original record IDs **exactly**. They validate
the ID without trimming it; normalization applies only to editable display
text, never stored identity keys.

Inventory edits now generate **sparse patches** rather than resending every
visible field. Omitted or unchanged values—including original registration/
chassis strings with spaces, notes, purchase timestamps and costs—are not
reformatted, cleared or written again. Blank historical numeric values cannot
silently erase original values; these require separate reconciliation. No-op
updates are refused without sending a network request. Price changes still
require the separate owner-confirmed price-history workflow, and stock status
changes remain confined to the existing sale/reconciliation flow.

These safeguards are synthetic development tests only. No real Owner cloud
editing, hosted D1/R2 changes, source-import execution or production release
has occurred. All activation flags remain disabled.

# Release-readiness report — 14 October 2026

**Project:** private Naina Motors Dealer Desk CRM, existing Sites Version 15 live; separate showroom must remain untouched.  
**Scope:** current GitHub feature branch and the exported Version 16 source, **not** live deployment or cloud cutover.

## Verified in the available container
- Node.js 22.16.0 and npm 10.9.2 were available.
- Source export: `Naina_Motors_Dealer_Desk_V16_GitHub_Ready.zip`. This predates GitHub's Step 26 feature commits. Do not confuse baseline test results with tests of the full current feature branch.
- **60/60** baseline pure Node browser/local-storage/management/media/vehicle-context/cloud tests passed on the exported Version 16 source (test files: `local-storage.test.mjs`, `management-ui.test.mjs`, `vehicle-context.test.mjs`, `media-ui.test.mjs`, `cloud.test.mjs`).
- Portable static preflight validated **28/28** applicable checks on the original export. On a disposable local fixture with the development preview route and disabled gate added, strict preflight passed **31/31** checks and correctly failed when the preview gate was changed to `true`. Its two new built-in Node regression tests passed **2/2** locally.
- The **actual current GitHub branch** was independently checked through GitHub: all **10 HTML-referenced browser assets** exist; all referenced JavaScript files parse. Four release flags were fetched from the development branch and each remains `false`.
- No private business JSON was imported into D1, uploaded to GitHub, or used as test data.

## Build and complete test blockers
- The exported source has **no `node_modules`**. `npm run build` fails before compilation because `node_modules/vinext/dist/cli.js` is unavailable. This does NOT establish a source-code compilation failure.
- External npm registry access failed with `EAI_AGAIN` (DNS/network unavailable in this container). The framework dependencies cannot currently be installed here, so **no complete vinext production build** is claimed.
- Some original release-safety tests depend on a non-exported `source-data/imported-data.js` file and an original Git commit/history that is not present in the portable ZIP. These tests cannot serve as passing evidence in the exported checkout; don't fabricate or replace original business data.
- TypeScript/D1 bindings, original owner identity on hosted Sites, storage migration, R2 file-byte backup/restore, browser/iPhone synchronization and production rollback remain **unverified**.
- The current feature branch is NOT the same as the static exported ZIP; a proper checked-out branch with installed dependencies is required for full regression and build.

## Repeatable preflight and release commands
From the **Dealer Desk GitHub repository**, not the showroom:

```sh
npm run preflight:source
npm run test:preflight
npm run build
```

The first two commands are zero-dependency checks and do not contact D1/R2, delete files or alter the browser. The third requires a compatible installed lockfile dependency tree and the production framework.

## Non-negotiable release conditions
1. `preflight:source`, targeted and full regression suites, framework build and security tests pass against the **same specific feature commit**.
2. Original browser backup is exported and verified off-site, without changing the `naina-desk-v1` key.
3. Real owner-only identity, D1 schema migrations, R2 bucket binding and read/write isolation are tested on **disposable nonproduction resources**.
4. Vehicle/sale/customer/payment/expense IDs and accounting totals are reconciled before any import. Private photo/document files must be exported and SHA-256 verified independently of the database snapshot.
5. Perform a reversible test cutover and recovery rehearsal. Obtain separate deliberate authorization for any live data import/overwrite or live Sites deployment.
6. Keep all four server-side release switches disabled until all checks are satisfied.

**Current decision: BLOCKED for production release.** Continue development and offline verification in the draft PR; do not merge/deploy or enable cloud storage based on this report.

## Additional offline D1 migration verification

The exported Version 16 SQL files `drizzle/0000_deep_mockingbird.sql` and `drizzle/0001_private_dashboard_features.sql` were executed in Python SQLite `:memory:`, with foreign-key enforcement enabled. The check passed: **2 migration files, 27 tables, 18 explicit indexes, six critical unique indexes present, zero FK violations and `PRAGMA quick_check = ok`**. This was **not** a production Cloudflare D1 test.

The reproducible verification is saved as `scripts/verify-schema-sqlite.py` and exposed through `npm run verify:schema:offline` (requires Python 3 with standard-library `sqlite3`). It does not open a disk DB, connect to Cloudflare or mutate business records.

The original `tests/schema-additions.test.py` also contains tests that require the **original Git SHA** and installed `wrangler`; those prerequisites are absent from the export, so its full suite is **not green** in this container. Use the new independent in-memory schema verification while recording the old test limitations transparently.

## 14 October 2026 update — GitHub CI production build VERIFIED

The preceding local-container dependency blockage is **superseded for GitHub CI**, not for the old portable ZIP environment. On GitHub Actions workflow run **38599063469** (commit `0c20b3f4ffec7bc029094749954b6d3278d2eeb7`), the private Dealer Desk successfully:

- Installed the project's **frozen pnpm lockfile** using Node.js 22 and pnpm 11.25.0.
- Executed **250 non-legacy synthetic Node regression tests: 250 passed, 0 failed**.
- Passed `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`.
- Completed `pnpm exec vinext build` successfully. The builder reported “Build complete. Run vinext start to start the production server.”
- No production Sites deployment, D1/R2 provisioning or data import occurred.

The 38 failed tests from the **previous** run were traced to stale test harness mocks / assertions after integration changes, and corrected before the successful run. Do not claim that the old source-history-dependent `release-safety.test.mjs` ran: it remains intentionally excluded because the original Site Git SHA and excluded private source-data fixture are not available.

A subsequent workflow improvement at commit `aa22104c` also puts the source release-gate preflight and in-memory migration verification ahead of test/typecheck/build in GitHub Actions. **That additional workflow's success remains pending until its own run completes.**

**Release decision remains BLOCKED** pending hosted owner identity, real D1/R2 runtime access tests, verified 386-record migration reconciliation, complete independent backups, cross-device/iPhone security tests, and rehearsed reversible deployment. A passing production build alone is not a cloud cutover.

## 15 October 2026: strict financial date integrity in development

The CRM's existing single date validator now rejects **calendar-impossible**
YYYY-MM-DD dates even when a JavaScript runtime would silently normalize them
(e.g. February 30 -> March 2). This protects the persisted sale date, receipt
date and other `*_at` event dates before any atomic SQL batch or receipt is
written. The change preserves date-only entries and syntactically valid ISO
instant entries (including explicit time-zone offsets); real February 29 leap
days remain accepted. Regression tests assert that invalid sale and payment
dates leave inventory, customer-payment ledger, cashbook and cloud revision
**unchanged**. No browser legacy dates or source Excel values are rewritten.

This remains offline development evidence, NOT validation on hosted D1 or an
approved production release. Cloud switches stay disabled.
