ui/workspace-cloud.html.value:
NAINA MOTORS · PRIVATE OWNER WORKSPACE

Cloud workspace

Explicit cloud operations, separate from your browser-local CRM.

← Return to Dealer Desk
Cloud activation requires a separately approved release.

No records load automatically. This page never reads, clears, imports or overwrites browser localStorage. Your local CRM remains the working source until an approved migration. File selection alone does not upload.

Not checked. Cloud controls are locked.

Records & operations

Refresh retrieves current cloud records. Conflicts never overwrite another device's changes. Amounts are in rupees. Sales, payments, cashbook and price history are append-only. Edit expense totals through Vehicle expenses; record new sale through Sales and balance receipts through Customer payments. For vehicle location, use the vehicle ID as the record ID.

New record

Private vehicle media

Maximum upload 15 MB. JPEG, PNG and WebP previews. PDF and HEIC download only; no automatic conversion. Files remain attached after a sale. Archiving does not delete bytes.

Import preview & independent backup

Preview compares a chosen backup against cloud records. It does not import or switch the CRM. Restore verification validates a cloud snapshot; it does not restore data.

Media bytes must be backed up separately using each media item's download/export control. A database snapshot alone is not a complete media backup.

# Naina Motors Dealer Desk — unpublished cloud preparation

Existing Site: appgprj_6aca62581e288191af74309f0392facc
Domain: crm.nainamotors.com (no DNS or audience changes)

## Operating mode
The root route returns the original CRM HTML with a Cloud readiness link. The original app.js, stylesheet and imported-data.js are preserved byte-for-byte under public/. The original browser-storage behaviour stays active. Cloud readiness never reads, writes or clears browser localStorage.

The manifest declares D1 binding DB. Saving this version does not provision a hosted database or apply hosted migrations. Deployment needs separate user approval. Deployment applies schema only and cannot import business records. No cloud switch or business-data write endpoint is enabled.

## Owner security
Sites private sharing remains owner-only. Cloud endpoints additionally require the platform-injected authenticated identity and the verified existing owner's email allowlist. Stable platform userId is available for future audit ownership. Email changes or ownership changes require re-review of the allowlist before use. POST routes also require a same-origin Origin header. Service bypass tokens without visitor identity are not sufficient. No owner credentials are bundled in client code.

## Schema
Drizzle-generated migration 0000_deep_mockingbird.sql creates vehicles, sales, customers, leads, expenses, import_history, audit_logs, cloud_metadata and connection_probes. It contains only 9 CREATE TABLE and 4 CREATE UNIQUE INDEX statements. No seeds or data-changing migrations exist. Do not change applied migration history after deployment.

Full vehicle backup objects, including all original Excel fields, are designed to remain in payload_json. Parking and other expenses have separate expense kinds. Business import implementation and record mutation remain intentionally disabled pending separate approval; no automatic projection or correction occurs.

## Review workflow after separately approved deployment
1. Keep the private audience. Verify the original CRM still shows the owner's local records.
2. Open /cloud as the owner; refresh status and verify DB and all nine tables.
3. Run connection test. It atomically inserts, reads and removes a random isolated connection_probes row; it never changes business tables.
4. Select a current JSON backup and choose Preview only. The server performs read-only snapshot queries, validates records, classifies insert/update/skip/conflict and flags review rows. A dataset revision mismatch rejects preview. Existing changed records require matching per-record cloudRevision to be proposed as updates. Preview results include a backup hash and revision and are not persisted.
5. No import or cloud-switch button is present. POST /api/cloud/import returns 423. Business import and switching require a subsequent approved implementation with transaction-bound revision checks, audit entries, recovery and before/after reconciliation.

## Tests performed
- Production Vinext build: passed (root, /cloud and 5 cloud API routes).
- Node tests: authorization, CSRF origin, backups, duplicates, UNREG handling, revisions, review preservation, disabled imports.
- Local D1 emulator: schema applied; isolated probe insert/read/delete verified; business tables empty.
- Original CRM app.js, style.css, imported-data.js: exact byte comparison passed.
- Supplied version-3 backup dry run against empty data: 386 inserts, 0 updates, 0 skips, 0 conflicts; 3 flagged records (review is a subset, not extra records).
- No live hosted database test or browser visual QA performed. These remain deployment acceptance gates.

## Recovery
This unpublished version does not affect production. Keep the existing production version and JSON backup. After deployment, rolling application code back does not undo database schema; this schema is additive and creates only new empty tables. Never treat rollback as permission to discard business data.

name: Dealer Desk development checks
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: dealer-desk-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 12
    steps:
      - name: Checkout private Dealer Desk source
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Prepare pinned pnpm
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 11.25.0
          run_install: false
      - name: Node.js 22
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: pnpm
      - name: Install locked dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Verify source assets and production release locks
        run: pnpm run preflight:source
      - name: Verify offline D1 migrations and unique indexes
        run: python3 scripts/verify-schema-sqlite.py
      - name: Check actual ephemeral local D1 and R2 bindings using only fictional data
        run: node scripts/test-local-cloud-bindings.mjs
      - name: Run non-legacy Node regression tests
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mapfile -t tests < <(find tests -maxdepth 1 -name '*.test.mjs' ! -name 'release-safety.test.mjs' | sort)
          node --test "${tests[@]}"
      - name: Check TypeScript across project
        run: pnpm exec tsc --noEmit
      - name: Build development-only candidate
        run: pnpm exec vinext build
      - name: Exercise built local Worker and locked private API routes
        run: node scripts/smoke-built-worker.mjs

# Does not provision databases, deploy Sites, upload to R2, or use secrets.
# release-safety.test.mjs is an old site-commit fixture requiring private
# Git history and source-data/imported-data.js omitted from the safe export.
# A fresh production release audit is required before ever deploying.

docs/PRIVATE_RECOVERY_PAIR.md.value:
# Two-copy private cloud recovery equivalence gate (offline)

This augments the existing D1 snapshot and R2 byte-backup checks. It does **not**
authorize production migration or prove hosted disaster recovery.

## Purpose

Before trusting a new copy of the CRM's private cloud data, check **both**:
- All 27 D1 tables are present, internally checksummed and relationship-valid,
  and all row values are exactly equal between the two copies (order independent).
- All complete and archived private R2 documents/photos are present in both
  local folders as \`<media-id>.bin\`, with exact recorded SHA-256 and byte counts.
  No pending, missing, extra, corrupt or symlinked media file can pass.

Source and candidate export paths must be outside the Git checkout and distinct.
Neither input is modified. SQLite restoration and authentic hosted D1/R2
restoration are **not performed** by this particular command.

## Owner's private-computer command

Record each raw D1 export's independent SHA-256 **before** attempting recovery.
The digest must be of the exact raw JSON bytes, not the embedded signed value.

\`\`\`sh
node scripts/verify-private-recovery-pair.mjs /private/source-d1.json /private/source-media SOURCE_RAW_SHA256 /separate/candidate-d1.json /separate/candidate-media CANDIDATE_RAW_SHA256
\`\`\`

For Windows PowerShell, use absolute paths, preferably in separate
Owner-controlled private folders. For example, compute each digest with
\`(Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 "C:\Private\source-d1.json").Hash.ToLowerInvariant()\`.
Do not paste actual private digests, records, file names or personal details
into GitHub, CI logs or public chats. All CLI output is aggregate-only.

The process exits with code 0 only for two individually complete media bundles
with the same full D1 records. If the snapshots' \`exportedAt\` times differ but
all 27 table rows are identical, the content is considered identical.
If even one table's rows differ, it reports only the affected **table names**
and fails; it never prints source record IDs, registration numbers or customers.

## What this gate cannot claim

Two directories on one laptop are not independent offsite backups. A
matching copy does not establish origin, verified custody or point-in-time
consistency of real hosted D1/R2 exports. This tool does not restore SQLite
tables, write D1 or R2, deploy production code, test true Owner authentication,
or check iPhone/laptop behavior. Run the separate isolated SQLite restore
rehearsal with \`node scripts/verify-cloud-restore.mjs\` on each genuine snapshot,
and test hosted restores into separately isolated staging with authenticated
media downloads **before** cloud production activation.

No source or destination backup file should be committed to the repo.


## Aliased file protection

Two backup folders are not two copies if they contain hard links to the same
database or media bytes. This verifier explicitly refuses shared device/inode
identities for a pair of database snapshots **and for every media file**; it
also refuses symbolic-linked input files/directories and other special media
entries. This is a local identity check, **not** proof of different physical
disks, geographically independent/offsite storage, historical authenticity or
a successful hosted recovery. Those gates remain separate.


## One-command offline recovery readiness (recommended)

When both private copies have been independently exported and their *original
raw JSON SHA-256* values retained separately, run:

\`\`\`sh
node scripts/verify-private-recovery-readiness.mjs /absolute/source-d1.json /absolute/source-media SOURCE_RAW_SHA256 /absolute/candidate-d1.json /absolute/candidate-media CANDIDATE_RAW_SHA256
\`\`\`

This performs the paired 27-table relationship/content comparison and **both**
byte-for-byte archived/active media audits, then runs the strict disposable
SQLite schema, foreign key, integrity and row-round-trip rehearsal independently
for **each** D1 snapshot. A single command avoids running the paired backup
tool and the SQLite restore tool separately for both inputs.

A zero exit code means these checks passed **locally**, not that cloud restore
or offsite custody is proven. It never accesses the hosted CRM or performs
persistent writes. It always returns \`releaseReady:false\`; real Owner ingress,
staging isolation, payment reconciliation, hosted D1/R2 recovery, laptop/iPhone
tests and production authorization remain open. Do not commit any backup files
or export their sensitive contents into this repository.
